::: {.callout-important}

I've given up on making a comprehensive / canonical list of the NPI , Medicaid billing and Medicaid provider numbers. This is especially a problem with the billing and the money -- they just don't match. Instead, I'm just going to work on it by name -- who is it that is identified in the NC Tracks data? This will involve going through the list of names and making them standardized for our purposes. 

To do this again: Make sure to correct the Clear Creek NPI from the licensing data if we're using it. It's wrong there. See the Excel sheet saved here for the right one (it's not called Clear Creek there - it's called )

::: 


```{r}
#| label: setup

pacman::p_load("tidyverse", "janitor", "here", "lubridate", "readxl", "glue", "data.table", "arrow", "duckdb")
here::i_am("money.qmd")



```


## Rate sheets


## Get the payments made FY 2023-FY 2025 

There is no record yet for FY 2026, which ended June 30, 2026. 

I checked, and there are no provider classifications that are different than rendering classficiations for the purpose of ICFs. THere is only one classification for ICFs - They're considered custodial care, not residential treatment. 

```{r}
#| label: load-money

full_money <- readRDS("nctracks/icf_payments_3year.RDS")  |> 
  filter (rendering_taxonomy_code == "315P00000X")

```

Check the names and npis of the billing and rendering providers: 

```{r}
#| label: count-names



full_money |> 
  group_by ( billing_npi_atypical, billing_provider_name, billing_provider_dba_name, 
             rendering_npi_atypical, rendering_provider_name, fiscal_year) |> 
  summarize ( payment_recs = n() , 
              amount = sum(num_amount_paid), 
              .groups = "drop") |> 
  



```

## Match against the rate sheets

I'm not sure if these NPIs match the rate sheets, so let's see how many of them we can get matched. 

I'm using the 9/30/2025 rate sheet - there is one for 2022, but nothing in between. I can go back and look - there was an increase then a decrease due to covid and medicaid expansion, but it's not showing up in the data. This will be a wild estimate just to make sure that we have them matched up. 


Two documents are from 2022, which I will use for 2023-2024. Then there are a series of documents for 2025, and I can't quite figure out what is changed. They do add new NPI's and there are no other identifiers that we can use from the names, so it's important to get those right. 

These used to be identified by the name of the facility, which may or may not be standardized. I need to get them into some form that I can use. The easiest way to do this is frankly by hand, using the list that Malena figured out. I've done that on an Excel workbook.

Take the July 22, 2025 rate sheet, which should reflect what the previous rates were. Concatenate the duplicate NPIs. (There is also one on 9/30/2025 that has a note that says "8% rate reduciton" on a bunch of the rows, but then a later one seems to remove it, so I can't tell if it was reduced or not. I'm using this one, since it would have been after the FY 2025. We don't have a rate sheet for the actual fiscal years.)

```{r}
#| label: load-rate-sheets

rate_sheet <- readRDS("nctracks/all_rates_by_npi_2025.RDS") |> 
  filter ( source_file == "icf_2025_07_22") |> 
  # there are 5 dupes for homes that are basically thes ame places (sand ridge, for example)
  summarize ( across ( 
                  everything() , 
                  \(x) paste (unique(x), collapse="; ")  
                  ), 
            .by = npi
            )


```
(Goes from 337 to 334 rows)


```{r}
#| label: get-xl-2022


icfrates_2022_raw <- read_excel("nctracks/icfrates/icfrates_2022_02_09.xlsx" , 
                  range="B7:L343"  , col_names = c("npi", "blank", "provider_id", "provider_name", "chain_rate", "covid15", "accomodation",
                                                  "npi2", "covid05", "covid10", "effective_2022"), 
                   col_types = c("text", "skip", "text", "text", "numeric", "numeric", "text", "text", "numeric", "numeric", "numeric")
              ) |> 
            summarize ( across ( 
                  everything() , 
                  \(x) paste (unique(x), collapse="; ")  
                  ), 
            .by = npi
             ) |> 
              select ( npi, provider_id, provider_name, chain_rate, npi2, effective_2022) 

icfrates_2022_raw |> 
  filter ( npi != npi2)

icf2022 <-
  icfrates_2022_raw |> 
  select ( npi22 = npi, provider22 = provider_id, name22 = provider_name, chain_rate, rate22 = effective_2022)


```
I have no idea what "chain rate" means -- whether it refers to a chain of providers, or if it refers to a chain that you multiply something by. 

Now merge them to get the rates and see what we have. (Org name is always blank)

```{r}
#| label: rates-match

rates <-
  rate_sheet |> 
  mutate ( rate25 = parse_number(rate), 
           eff_date25 = as.Date(eff_date)) |> 
  select ( npi, provider25 = provider, name25 = name,  rate25 , eff_date25) |> 
  full_join ( icf2022, join_by ( npi == npi22)) |> 
  filter ( !is.na(npi))



```
There doesn't appear to be any difference between the npis -- unlike later in 2025, there are no additional or removed npis from what I can tell ( 334 unique npis in both years)


## Check npis rates against the actual spending


```{r}
#| label: spending-npi-matched

full_money |> 
  rowid_to_column() |> 
  left_join ( rates, join_by ( billing_npi_atypical == npi) ) |> 
  arrange ( rowid)  |> 
  get_dupes(rowid)



```

No dupes on rowid so I can keep going



```{r}
#| label: get-money-spreadsheet

options(scipen=999)

money_with_rates <-
  full_money |> 
  filter ( !is.na(billing_npi_atypical)) |> 
  select ( fiscal_year, 
          payer , 
          billing_npi = billing_npi_atypical,
          billing_name = billing_provider_name, 
          billing_dba = billing_provider_dba_name, 
          billing_address, 
          rendering_npi = rendering_npi_atypical, 
          rendering_name = rendering_provider_name, 
          rendering_address , 
          recips = num_number_of_recipients, 
          visits = num_number_of_visits, 
          amount_paid = num_amount_paid,
          ) |> 
  left_join ( rates |>  select ( npi, medicaid_id = provider25, rate_name = name25 ,
                                 rate25, rate22), 
              join_by ( billing_npi == npi)
            ) |>  
  arrange (fiscal_year, billing_npi, desc(billing_name), desc(rendering_address)) |> 
  group_by ( fiscal_year, billing_npi) |> 
  mutate ( total_days = sum(visits, na.rm=TRUE) ,
           total_amt = sum( amount_paid, na.rm=TRUE), 
           missing_days = sum (is.na(visits)) , 
           missing_amts = sum(is.na(amount_paid))
  ) |> 
  slice_head (n=1) |> 
  select (fiscal_year, npi=billing_npi, 
          medicaid_id, billing_name, billing_dba,
          rendering_name, rendering_address,
          total_days, total_amt, missing_days, missing_amts, 
          rate25, rate22, rate_name) |> 
  mutate ( rate22 = parse_number(rate22) ) |> 
  ungroup()  
  
 


```

Let's just save it as a spreadsheet so they can look at it more easily


```{r}
#| label: save-excel

library(writexl)

writexl::write_xlsx(money_with_rates, "../analysis/money_with_rates.xlsx")

```
